<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **41** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 493a6c4a5f5b83d953f19092279abdf07b6f4017` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2011cd017b0f6979357d6b0a2bda4b0673f30720` — the merge of head `22f886e1d2be780b9b159b9fbcdfa98b0b4bcb45` into base `493a6c4a5f5b83d953f19092279abdf07b6f4017`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2011cd017b0f6979357d6b0a2bda4b0673f30720 && git checkout 2011cd017b0f6979357d6b0a2bda4b0673f30720
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 493a6c4a5f5b83d953f19092279abdf07b6f4017 22f886e1d2be780b9b159b9fbcdfa98b0b4bcb45 && git checkout -B drift-repro 493a6c4a5f5b83d953f19092279abdf07b6f4017 && git merge --no-ff 22f886e1d2be780b9b159b9fbcdfa98b0b4bcb45

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 493a6c4a5f5b83d953f19092279abdf07b6f4017
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 493a6c4a5f5b83d953f19092279abdf07b6f4017` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`RestProtocol` gains `getMetaItemsForExecution?`: RIGHT, a widening.** It is optional and typed as `MetadataProtocol['getMetaItems']`, so no protocol has to provide anything new. The dev measured rest's `dist/index.d.ts` at `cb0a2fcf` and at this head: the export list is unchanged (67 names), and outside doc comments that member is the only changed line. It is the list twin of `getMetaItemForExecution?`, which #24666 (`6464df3462`) declared the same way.
- **The gates' `object` list now reads the execution face: RIGHT, nothing served changes.** `getMetaItemsForExecution` and `getMetaItems` share `readFlattenedMetaItems` and differ only in the final serving decorations (`_diagnostics`, per-type redaction). So the set of items the nav-servability gate, the batch exposure gate and the by-name list fallback judge is the same set. Their readers take only `enable` and serve none of the list, which is the same posture as the by-name twin from #24666. The protocol's own warning against serving the execution face from a door holds, because no answer carries those items. `book` and `doc` stay on the served face. The request shape (`type`, optional `environmentId`) is the one `getMetaItems` takes. The runtime dispatcher's `MetaDomainProtocol` is not a barrel export: an internal type, no published surface.
- **`computeMetadataDiagnostics` memo: RIGHT, no accept-set change.** The verdict is keyed by the schema object (a `WeakMap`, so a replaced schema starts empty) and by a SHA-256 of a faithful encoding of the stripped document. A document with no faithful key is parsed every time. Each caller gets its own copy, and the memo is bounded LRU at 4096 per schema. The accepted and refused documents are unchanged; only repeat parses are skipped. The dev hashed the served bytes of six types before and after, and they are SHA-256-identical. `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` and `@objectstack/runtime` declarations are byte-identical at both ends, so `Clause-②: no` holds for them.

### ② Semver level

All three packages are `patch`, which is right. `Metadata-protocol: none` makes `patch` the level (AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3; ruling A on #25105), and `check-changeset-no-major` refuses a `minor` under `none`. rest's own changeset carries `Clause-②: yes (widening)` with the before/after reading. The metadata-protocol and runtime changeset carries `Clause-②: no`. Both declaration lines are in the PR body, which the seat edited through the relay.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions[0]` (the card's ≤15 ms and ≤5% targets): answered by ruling A 6408692677. The targets are relaxed to the measured numbers, and `Closes #25783` is right.
- The declaration flag the seat raised on `bb46886e` (`Clause-②: no` should be `yes (widening)`) is fixed on this head, which changes changesets only (`git diff bb46886e..22f886e1`: 2 `.changeset` files).
